waterQualityEngine.paramOutOfRange: {{param}} is out of the recommended range.

explanations.phLow: Your water is too acidic (pH {{value}}). Acidic water can corrode pipes and leach metals like lead and copper into your water, which can be harmful. Safe range is 6.5–8.5.
explanations.phHigh: Your water is too alkaline (pH {{value}}). Very alkaline water can taste bitter and may irritate skin. Safe range is 6.5–8.5.
explanations.tdsLow: Total Dissolved Solids ({{value}} mg/L) is unusually low, which may mean mineral content is stripped out — like some over-filtered water.
explanations.tdsHigh: Total Dissolved Solids is {{value}} mg/L — above the recommended 600 mg/L. High TDS can indicate salts, minerals, or contaminants dissolved in the water.
explanations.turbidityLow: Turbidity ({{value}} NTU) is fine — clear water.
explanations.turbidityHigh: Your water is cloudy or murky (turbidity {{value}} NTU). Cloudy water may contain particles, sediment or microorganisms. It should be filtered or boiled before drinking.
explanations.chlorineLow: Chlorine level ({{value}} mg/L) is too low. Tap water needs some chlorine to kill bacteria. Below 0.2 mg/L means bacteria may survive in the water.
explanations.chlorineHigh: Chlorine level ({{value}} mg/L) is higher than recommended. Very high chlorine can taste and smell unpleasant and may cause digestive discomfort.
explanations.conductivityLow: Conductivity is very low — this is usually fine for drinking water.
explanations.conductivityHigh: Conductivity ({{value}} µS/cm) is high, suggesting dissolved minerals or salts above recommended levels.
explanations.oxygenLow: Dissolved oxygen ({{value}} mg/L) is below 5 mg/L, which may indicate stagnant or contaminated water.
explanations.hardnessLow: Water hardness is very low — soft water. This is generally fine but can be slightly more corrosive.
explanations.hardnessHigh: Water hardness ({{value}} mg/L) is quite high. Hard water causes scale build-up and may affect taste but is not usually a health risk.
explanations.bacteriaHigh: Bacteria detected ({{value}} CFU/100mL). This water is not safe to drink without boiling or purification.
explanations.temperatureHigh: Water temperature ({{value}}°C) is above 25°C. Warm water promotes bacterial growth — store and use cold.

cloudy.title: Water appears cloudy or milky
cloudy.explanation: Cloudy water (also called turbid) usually means suspended particles or air. If the cloudiness settles, it may just be air. If it remains, there could be sediment or contaminants.

yellowish.title: Water has a yellowish tint
yellowish.explanation: Yellow water often indicates iron, manganese or organic matter. It can also come from rusty pipes. Not safe to drink without testing.

brownish.title: Water appears brown or rusty
brownish.explanation: Brown water often signals corroded pipes, iron deposits or disturbed sediment. This is a serious infrastructure or contamination concern.

greenish.title: Water has a greenish colour
greenish.explanation: Green water can indicate algae growth (especially in well/tank water) or copper corrosion in pipes. Avoid drinking without treatment.

reddish.title: Water appears reddish
reddish.explanation: Red or orange tints often mean high iron content or pipe corrosion. This is a sign to investigate your plumbing.

rotten_eggs.title: Rotten egg smell detected
rotten_eggs.explanation: A rotten-egg smell means hydrogen sulphide gas — produced by bacteria in water with no oxygen, or by sulphur deposits. Do not drink without treatment.

metallic.title: Metallic smell or taste
metallic.explanation: A metallic odour often means high iron, copper or lead content, possibly from corroding pipes. Have your plumbing inspected.

chlorine.title: Strong chlorine smell
chlorine.explanation: A strong chlorine smell usually means your tap water treatment plant has added more chlorine than usual. At normal levels it is safe, but if very strong, let water sit for a few minutes before drinking.

earthy.title: Earthy or musty smell
earthy.explanation: An earthy smell often comes from algae or organic matter — common in well water or surface water sources. May need filtration.

chemical.title: Chemical smell detected
chemical.explanation: A chemical odour can indicate industrial contamination or excessive disinfection by-products. Do NOT drink this water until tested.

stopDrinking.reason: Serious quality issues were detected that could cause illness.

boil3min.action: Boil water for at least 3 minutes before any use
boil3min.reason: Boiling kills most bacteria and parasites.

useBottled.action: Use bottled water or an alternative safe source for drinking and cooking
useBottled.reason: Until the issue is resolved, bottled water is the safest option.

boil5min.action: Boil water for at least 5 minutes or use water purification tablets
boil5min.reason: Bacteria were detected. Boiling or chemical purification will make the water safe.

callPlumber.action: Contact a plumber or your water authority to inspect your pipes
callPlumber.reason: Infrastructure issues (rust, leaks, stains) can contaminate water at the point of use.

flushPipes.action: Run your tap for 2–3 minutes before using water
flushPipes.reason: Flushing the pipes removes stagnant or rust-coloured water and brings fresher water from the main supply.

airChlorine.action: Fill a jug with water and leave it uncovered for 30 minutes
airChlorine.reason: Chlorine naturally dissipates when exposed to air, reducing the taste and smell.

getLabTest.action: Consider getting a certified water test from your local health authority
getLabTest.reason: A lab test will confirm exactly what is in your water so the right solution can be found.

inspectOldPipes.action: Have an old pipe inspection done by a qualified plumber
inspectOldPipes.reason: Pipes older than 20 years may contain lead solder or be corroding, which can contaminate drinking water.

regularTesting.action: Continue regular water testing every 6–12 months
regularTesting.reason: Even safe water can change over time due to pipe ageing, seasonal changes or local events.

homeFilter.action: Consider a home water filter (e.g. activated carbon jug filter)
homeFilter.reason: Filters can improve taste, remove chlorine odour, and catch trace contaminants.

contactCliniq.action: Contact Water Cliniq for a certified laboratory test and professional water treatment
contactCliniq.reason: Water Cliniq provides accredited analysis and on-site treatment. Only a lab test can confirm exact contaminant levels and guarantee safety.

summaries.safe: Your {{source}} is safe to drink. {{detail}} Continue testing periodically.
summaries.safeDetail: All checked parameters are within WHO safe ranges.
summaries.safeDetailMinor: There are minor points to watch but nothing requiring immediate action.
summaries.caution: Your {{source}} is NOT safe to drink without treatment. {{count}} concern{{plural}} found. Boil or filter before drinking.
summaries.unsafe: Your {{source}} is NOT safe to drink. Do not consume it without boiling or purification first. {{count}} serious issue{{plural}} identified — see the actions below.
summaries.dangerous: Your {{source}} is DANGEROUS. Stop drinking it immediately. {{count}} critical issue{{plural}} detected — find an alternative water source now.

tastes.bitter: A bitter taste can indicate high mineral content, chlorination by-products, or contamination. Avoid drinking until checked.
tastes.salty: Salty-tasting water may have high sodium or chloride content — sometimes from saltwater intrusion or softener run-off.
tastes.metallic: A metallic taste usually means high iron, copper or lead — often from ageing pipes. Have your plumbing tested.
tastes.sweet: A sweet taste is unusual and could indicate algae or dissolved minerals. Investigate the source.
tastes.chemical: A chemical taste is a serious warning sign of industrial contamination or disinfection by-products. Do NOT drink.
tastes.other: An unusual taste warrants investigation — have the water tested by a certified lab.
tastes.unknown: Unusual taste detected — have the water tested.
